passage:
Naveen: chassis moves!! straight line works
Pema: does it turn?
Naveen: left is fine, right drifts 🙂
Pema: fix the right wheel first, no sensors yet
Naveen: agreed. if we bolt sensors on now we won't know if it's wiring or wheels
Pema: exactly. one thing at a time
Naveen: tightened the right wheel, it turns clean now
Pema: nice. now add ONE sensor and test
Naveen: done. it stops at the black line!
Pema: second one tomorrow
Naveen: so if it breaks we know it's the last thing we added
Pema: yep. and we always have a working robot to go back to 👍

qa.q: Which turn drifted on the chassis?
qa.a: Turning right drifted, while left was fine.

qa.q: Why does Naveen want to wait before adding sensors?
qa.a: Naveen worries the team would not know whether a fault is in the wiring or the wheels, and wants to trace problems easily.

qa.q: What could the team do if the second sensor breaks things?
qa.a: They could take the last sensor off and test again, since the base already worked.

qa.q: How might Pema see the step-by-step approach?
qa.a: Pema agrees and probably feels reassured, since every test builds on something already proven.

grounding: The team builds a basic chassis that moves and turns before adding sensors, so each new part is tested on something that already works.

subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: building a minimum working prototype first [Action]
passage: In the tin-roofed lab of the government school in Chittur, Mridul had already laid out the ultrasonic sensor, the colour sensor and a buzzer on newspaper. "Let's fix all of it today!" Lavanya slid the sensors gently to one side. "First it has to move. Just the chassis, two motors, the battery, one switch." It took them two evenings. On the second, the robot finally rolled across the cement floor and turned left when Mridul pressed the key. Then they added the colour sensor, only that, and tested again. It spun in circles. Because everything else had worked the day before, they knew the fault was in the new wiring, and found it in five minutes: a loose ground wire. Mridul laughed. "If we'd added everything at once, we'd still be searching."

qa.q: What floor did the robot roll across?
qa.a: It rolled across the cement floor.

qa.q: Why did Lavanya slide the sensors aside?
qa.a: Lavanya felt cautious and calm about it, wanting a base that moved first so any later fault would be easy to trace.

qa.q: What else could the pair do before adding the next part?
qa.a: They could note down what works after each step, so any new fault can be traced to the last change.

qa.q: How does Lavanya's approach look to Mridul by the end?
qa.a: Mridul first wanted everything at once, but by the end sees that building on a working base made the loose wire easy to find.

grounding: Shows a team getting a bare chassis to move and turn before adding sensors, so a new fault is quickly traced to the new part.

subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: building a minimum working prototype first [Action]
passage: The robotics club room in Toronto smelled of solder and cold pizza. Xin wanted to start with the gripper arm, the exciting part. Zeynep shook her head. "Wheels first. If it can't drive in a square, nothing else matters." By Wednesday their bare chassis could drive a taped square on the floor, three times out of three. On Thursday they bolted on the gripper. The first time it closed, the whole robot stopped dead. "It was fine yesterday," Xin said, "so it's the gripper." They measured: the gripper motor was pulling too much from the same battery. On Friday they gave it a separate battery pack, and the robot drove the square and picked up a paper cup. Xin wrote on the whiteboard in big letters: "One new thing at a time."

qa.q: What could the chassis do by Wednesday?
qa.a: It could drive a taped square on the floor, three times out of three.

qa.q: Why did Zeynep insist on wheels first?
qa.a: Zeynep felt sure that everything depended on driving and was wary of building the exciting part on something untested.

qa.q: What would you advise the team before adding the next part?
qa.a: Test the robot on the square after each addition and note what changed, so faults stay easy to trace.

qa.q: How does Zeynep's plan look to Xin by Friday?
qa.a: Xin, who wanted the gripper first, ends up writing the lesson on the whiteboard, showing Xin now values adding one new thing at a time.

grounding: Illustrates a team building a chassis that drives reliably before adding a gripper, so the new fault is traced quickly to the new part.
